data.body:
FIX MERGED. Gerrit change 2618 ('Re-sample a stalled repo-isolation git probe') reached LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 on patchset 3 and was submitted; it is on main.

ROOT CAUSE, established on evidence rather than elimination, and it corrected MY premise in this
ticket. I wrote that the blamed test 'provisions a real Node toolchain and is the heaviest thing in
the suite'. It does not -- it drives a shell STUB npm ('mkdir -p node_modules; exit 0') under tmp_path
and is one of the CHEAPEST tests in the file. Right conclusion (contention), wrong mechanism, and my
mechanism would have aimed a fix at the test instead of the probe.

What actually settled it:
 - '<Popen: returncode: -9 ...>' in the traceback: the child was ALIVE and killed by the timeout.
   Running, not wedged.
 - 400 [rebar-ci-timing] warnings in the same run, topping out at 4.562s on a DIFFERENT worker.
   Ordinary fixture setup on that runner reaches 91% of the probe's fixed 5s bound. The bound sits
   inside the runner's own latency distribution.
So the defect is THE BOUND, not the test: one fixed-timeout sample of a read-only, idempotent probe
taken ~19,000 times, three xdist workers deep, across a 45-minute run.

Reading (b) -- a leaked process or handle -- was ruled out at MECHANISM level: no real npm/esbuild
child exists to leak; 'git rev-parse HEAD' takes NO lock; a patched clock is impossible because
CPython binds 'from time import monotonic as _time' in subprocess; and a leaked PATH was ruled out
experimentally, since monkeypatch is function-scoped and finalizes before the autouse guard's
post-yield.

THE FIX: _run_git_probe re-samples a timed-out attempt up to GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS = 3, with the FINAL
attempt OUTSIDE the retry loop so a persistent TimeoutExpired propagates unconditionally -- loudness
is structural, not a conditional a later edit could invert. No sleep between attempts: the elapsed
per-attempt timeout IS the backoff, and sleeping would re-introduce the patched-time.sleep hazard
_stable_subprocess_time exists to defend against.

AC1 cause established (above). AC2 verified by workflow_dispatch against the schedule-gated job (run
33855430270): sweep (macos, full suite) = SUCCESS; before 19243 passed + 1 ERROR, after 19244 passed
with 0 errors. AC3 guard not weakened -- mutating head/porcelain to swallow TimeoutExpired FAILS 3
tests, and the real-HEAD-move detectors still fire. AC4 honoured: the e2e test is UNTOUCHED -- not
skipped, not marked, not excluded, which mattered given how often 'absence of execution reported as
success' turned up tonight. AC5 defect-seeded RED in 25 seconds rather than a 45-minute run:
'subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 0.484 seconds', green after.

Patchset 3 was needed because patchset 2 failed pytest ubuntu py3.12 -- a reminder that a change to
tests/_isolation.py touches the autouse guard on EVERY test, not just macOS.
